author: Kantoftes
quote:
This doesn't feel like a true GTA game anymore. It feels as though the series has gradually abandoned the very identity that made it one of the most iconic and influential franchises in gaming history. It has lost the rebellious spirit, unapologetic satire, dark humor, and raw personality that once defined Grand Theft Auto. Instead, it comes across as overly woke, sanitized, and afraid to push boundaries or offend anyone. The unfiltered humor and controversial social commentary that made the older titles so memorable seem to have been replaced by a much safer and more restrained approach.

While the open world is still enjoyable to explore on a surface level, it lacks the genuine freedom, unpredictability, and sense of absolute chaos that made previous entries so special. Older GTA games made you feel like you could do practically anything, stumble upon ridiculous situations, and create unforgettable moments without constantly feeling guided or restricted by the experience. Here, much of that spontaneity seems to be missing. The world may look impressive, but graphical fidelity and map size mean very little if the actual experience doesn't capture the spirit of the franchise.

What disappoints me most is the complete lack of memorable moments. I am already twelve hours into the game, and it still hasn't delivered a single sequence that made me feel the raw emotion, adrenaline, excitement, or sheer unpredictability I experienced countless times in previous installments. There is no moment that has genuinely shocked me, no mission that has left me wanting to immediately jump back in, and no memorable action sequence that makes me think, "This is what GTA is all about."

A GTA game should make you feel like you're part of a living, breathing criminal underworld, where absurdity, violence, satire, freedom, and chaos coexist naturally. It should be outrageous, unpredictable, occasionally offensive, and, above all, entertaining. It shouldn't feel like it's constantly trying to play things safe or appeal to absolutely everyone at the expense of its original identity.

I don't expect every new GTA to be a carbon copy of its predecessors, nor am I against innovation or change. But there is a difference between evolving a franchise and stripping away the characteristics that made it special in the first place. At this point, it genuinely feels like the developers have prioritized presentation and accessibility over substance and personality. And that's what makes it so disappointing. I didn't want another generic, polished open-world experience with a GTA logo attached to it. I wanted GTA. And fifteen hours in, I'm still waiting to find it, I really hope they start caring about the community more than the money!
